policy_name: Framework of an Acceptable Use Policy for External Generative AI
issuing_authority: Financial Services Information Sharing and Analysis Center (FS-ISAC)

key_dates.event: Published as part of FS-ISAC's series of AI risk white papers ('Illustrative for Adaptation')

covered_activities: employee use of external generative AI
conditions: Template to be adapted; offers permissive and stringent options
objective: Provides financial firms with an adaptable template, including sample policy text, for an acceptable use policy governing staff use of external generative AI, addressing data going into the systems (confidentiality, access, monitoring) and output coming out (accuracy, attribution, representation).

related_policies.policy: FS-ISAC 'Financial Services and AI: Leveraging the Advantages, Managing the Risks' (2024 white paper series)

conflict_rule: Non-binding template; firms adapt it subject to applicable law, regulation and internal policies.

clauses.original_text: The policy should cover external generative AI services used by staff regardless of how they are accessed (e.g., web interfaces, APIs, browser plug-ins or features embedded in other software).
clauses.object: acceptable use policy for external generative AI
clauses.requirement: apply the acceptable use policy to all external generative AI services irrespective of access route
clauses.purpose: avoid gaps in coverage of shadow or embedded generative AI use
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase reconstructed from search-result excerpts and secondary summaries; the official PDF (fsisac.com) could not be fetched, so wording and exact section placement are unverified. The document is a template offering permissive and stringent options, so modality is SHOULD. Examples of access routes are illustrative and not confirmed in the text.

clauses.section: Data provided to generative AI systems – Confidentiality
clauses.original_text: Employees should not provide confidential, proprietary, customer or other non-public firm information to external generative AI systems; this restriction may be relaxed where contracts give the firm control over how its data is protected at the vendor.
clauses.requirement: do not enter confidential/non-public data into external generative AI unless contractual data-protection controls exist
clauses.exception: contractual arrangements giving the firm control over vendor-side protection of its data
clauses.purpose: protect confidentiality (CIA triad) of firm and customer data
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase reconstructed from search-result excerpts and secondary summaries; the official PDF (fsisac.com) could not be fetched, so wording and exact section placement are unverified. The document is a template offering permissive and stringent options, so modality is SHOULD. The contractual-relaxation exception is corroborated by a search excerpt of the PDF.

clauses.section: Data provided to generative AI systems – Access
clauses.original_text: The firm should determine which staff may use external generative AI tools and from where (e.g., firm-managed devices and networks), choosing between permissive and stringent approaches.
clauses.object: access to external generative AI tools
clauses.requirement: define authorized users and access locations/devices for external generative AI
clauses.purpose: control data exposure and monitor use
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase reconstructed from search-result excerpts and secondary summaries; the official PDF (fsisac.com) could not be fetched, so wording and exact section placement are unverified. The document is a template offering permissive and stringent options, so modality is SHOULD.

clauses.section: Data received from generative AI systems (accuracy, attribution, representation)
clauses.original_text: Output from external generative AI should be reviewed for accuracy before use, attributed appropriately, and not be represented as an official position of the firm without the usual review and approval.
clauses.action: verify, attribute and control representation of
clauses.requirement: check output accuracy, attribute AI-generated content, and avoid presenting it as firm communications without review
clauses.purpose: output integrity and reputational/legal risk control
clauses.affected_asset: firm reputation; customers relying on communications
